== Biography ==

The March Hare is an inhabitant of Wonderland, described by the Cheshire Cat as mad. Alice speculates that his madness may be seasonal, less pronounced in May than it was in March.

The March Hare hosts a tea party beneath a tree outside his house, where he takes tea with the Hatter and a sleeping Dormouse, whom they use as a cushion. When Alice joins them, he offers her wine in an encouraging tone, though only tea sits on the table. He grows weary of their conversation and interrupts to suggest they change the subject, yawning as he does so. His manner exemplifies the peculiar logic of Wonderland—he offers wine with apparent sincerity despite the absence of any wine to serve.

== Relationships ==

'''[[Hatter]]''' — strained friendship. The two share the tea table, though their dynamic seems marked by tension.

'''[[Dormouse]]''' — acquaintance. The sleeping Dormouse sits between them at tea.

'''[[Alice]]''' — acquaintance. The March Hare remarked upon the impropriety of Alice sitting down at his table without having been invited.

* [[Hatter]] — Strained friendship (ch.7→ch.11)<ref>Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, chapter 7</ref>
